concept.name: Expansion
concept.definition: A broadening of price swings and bar ranges, reflecting rising volatility as one side of the market gains decisive control. It is the counterpart of compression and typically accompanies breakouts, breakdowns, and trend acceleration.
concept.intuition: The coiled spring releases: small quiet bars give way to large directional ones.
concept.mechanics: Observed as enlarging bar ranges and directional closes, often from a prior consolidation; quantified by widening Bollinger Bands (bands expand as the standard deviation of price rises) or rising ATR/BandWidth.
concept.failure_modes: Expansion driven by news spikes can be one-bar events that immediately mean-revert; chasing expansion late buys the extreme of the move.
concept.misconceptions: That expansion confirms a durable new trend; an initial volatility burst can be exhaustion rather than initiation.
concept.example: After weeks of narrow ranges, a stock prints consecutive wide-range up bars on heavy volume as it breaks out of its base — a volatility expansion phase.
